rawFindings.title: Duplicate CLI options are propagated as arrays instead of using the last value
rawFindings.explanation: When an option is provided more than once, optimist returns an array for that property. This assignment now copies that array directly into `options`, so duplicate scalar options such as `--port` or `--log-level` are no longer normalized. The later type conversions only handle strings, so `logLevel` remains an array and `port` remains an array instead of the last supplied value.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore normalization before assignment, e.g. assign `Array.isArray(argv[name]) ? argv[name].pop() : argv[name]`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Running `karma start --port 12 --port 34 --log-level info --log-level debug` produces `options.port === [12, 34]` and `options.logLevel === ['info', 'debug']` instead of `34` and `LOG_DEBUG`.
